explanation: Three ecological models describe the dynamics of succession: 1) Facilitation Model: each successive stage of species facilitates the invasion and establishment of the next stage of organisms. In this model, succession in a given area always leads to a predictable, stable climax community. 2) Inhibition Model: early colonists establish themselves and actively inhibit the growth and establishment of other plant species. Succession only proceeds when these colonists are damaged or die. 3) Tolerance Model: different types of plants can colonize a disturbed area at the same time, with chance playing the major role in determining which seeds arrive and establish first.

questions.q: According to the facilitation model of succession, what is the ultimate result of succession in a given area?
opts: A random assortment of transient species
A stable climax community that is always the same type
Total desertification due to resource depletion
The complete elimination of pioneer species by inhibition
questions.exp: The notes state that under the Facilitation Model, 'Succession in a particular area will always lead to the same type of community, a climax community.'

questions.q: Which succession model states that early colonists actively prevent the growth of other plants until those colonists die or are damaged?
questions.exp: The notes define the Inhibition Model as: 'Colonists remain and inhibit growth of other plants until the colonists are damaged or die.'
